findings.summary: RK-3 and RK-9 values verified; RK-9 independent.
findings.evidence: Omega_H = s/(2u+), s=0.9: Python Decimal prec 50 gives 0.31339450313662924709..., which rounds to 0.31339450313662925, the design doc line 95/350 literal; float64 also 0.3133945031366293. RK-3 = 2 matches doc line 88 (equator static limit 2 = 1.0 r_s).

findings.summary: static_limit is now the constant Decimal(2); it weakens oracle independence for RK-3 and the RK-18 static-limit-km row.
findings.evidence: A real bug in an eventual formula could not appear here. Acceptable: the doc defines RK-3 as a spin identity, DOC literals and the RK-18 anchor pin it, and the spin_value validation is retained and tested. Dropping cos_theta is a defensible YAGNI call, but the off-equator Chandrasekhar formula (doc line 116) loses its Python oracle and should be re-added with an off-equator anchor when K1.x needs staticLimitR(s, cosTheta).

findings.summary: The cleanup line the controller added is untested and is the only thing preventing a temp leak.
findings.evidence: With 'rm -rf $tmp' removed, the suite still passes and leaks 7 dirs per run in $TMPDIR, because the single EXIT trap is re-set each drill and only covers the last dir. Harmless at ~3 KB each but accumulates on a shared rig. A fix would be one parent mktemp -d with a single trap.

findings.summary: Instrument self-checks (cmp -s no-op guard, grep -F reason check) are themselves unverified; the six-decimal kill label depends on DOC dict order.
findings.evidence: Disabling either leaves the suite green. The six-decimal drill greps "doc literal: ('RK-10'", which holds only because RK-10 is the first DOC key.

findings.summary: The nan drill is killed by the ArithmeticError broadening, a behaviour change to an existing assert.
findings.evidence: Decimal NaN comparison raises InvalidOperation. The test now accepts it only when the message contains 'finite 0 <= spin < 1' (via the else/assert path), so a raw InvalidOperation from the oracle would fail the message assert: this is as intended. Covered by the ValueError-only mutation. Diff also changes check() to take an argument ($1 root), covered by this description.

Whole script about 2.7 s (check run 9 times), no network, no randomness, deterministic; mktemp under TMPDIR only. Low flake risk on a loaded rig. Change list matches the description: the only extra is the check() argument parameterisation and the success-line text update.
